1 Load the Data and Libraries

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, tidymodels, discrim, magrittr)
data <- read_rds("./data/data.rds")

2 Regression Models

2.1 Linear Regression With Interaction Term

# fit the model
lm_1 <- lm(X2 ~ X1*X3, data = data)

# fit with tidymodels
recipe_lm <- recipe(X2 ~ ., data = data) %>%
  step_interact(terms = ~ X1:X3)
recipe_lm %>% prep() %>% bake(new_data = NULL)
## # A tibble: 400 × 4
##       X1 X3       X2 X1_x_X31
##    <dbl> <fct> <dbl>    <dbl>
##  1 12.2  1      24.0    12.2 
##  2 13.7  1      25.3    13.7 
##  3 15.9  1      30.9    15.9 
##  4  8.60 1      15.8     8.60
##  5  7.95 1      12.1     7.95
##  6 12.0  1      21.9    12.0 
##  7  7.40 1      13.9     7.40
##  8  9.55 1      18.6     9.55
##  9 15.3  1      30.2    15.3 
## 10  5.79 1      10.2     5.79
## # ℹ 390 more rows
model_lm <- linear_reg() %>% 
  set_engine("lm")
workflow_lm <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(recipe_lm) %>%
  add_model(model_lm)
fit_lm <- workflow_lm %>%
  fit(data)
fit_lm %>% tidy()
## # A tibble: 4 × 5
##   term        estimate std.error statistic   p.value
##   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
## 1 (Intercept)    43.9     0.447       98.2 4.65e-280
## 2 X1             -1.51    0.0336     -45.1 5.10e-158
## 3 X31           -41.8     0.690      -60.6 2.21e-202
## 4 X1_x_X31        3.35    0.0527      63.6 4.96e-210
# model summary
 summary(lm_1)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = X2 ~ X1 * X3, data = data)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -6.5083 -1.1634 -0.0536  1.1394  6.5022 
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  43.88349    0.44701   98.17   <2e-16 ***
## X1           -1.51290    0.03356  -45.08   <2e-16 ***
## X31         -41.77327    0.68951  -60.58   <2e-16 ***
## X1:X31        3.35163    0.05267   63.63   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 2.082 on 396 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.9116, Adjusted R-squared:  0.9109 
## F-statistic:  1361 on 3 and 396 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
# tidymodels summary
fit_lm %>% extract_fit_parsnip() %>% pluck("fit") %>% summary()
## 
## Call:
## stats::lm(formula = ..y ~ ., data = data)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -6.5083 -1.1634 -0.0536  1.1394  6.5022 
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  43.88349    0.44701   98.17   <2e-16 ***
## X1           -1.51290    0.03356  -45.08   <2e-16 ***
## X31         -41.77327    0.68951  -60.58   <2e-16 ***
## X1_x_X31      3.35163    0.05267   63.63   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

metrics <- metric_set(rmse,rsq)
 (metrics_lm <- data %>% add_column(predict(fit_lm,data)) %>% metrics(truth = X2, estimate = .pred))
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   .metric .estimator .estimate
##   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
## 1 rmse    standard       2.07 
## 2 rsq     standard       0.912
 # visualise the data
 data %>%
 ggplot(aes(x = X1, y = X2, colour = X3)) +
 geom_point() +
 geom_smooth(method="lm")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

# check the assumptions
 plot(lm_1)

3 Classification Models

3.1 Support Vector Machine With Gaussian Radial Basis Function Kernel

# fit the model
svm_r <- recipe(X3 ~., data = data)
svm_m <- svm_rbf() %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")
svm_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(svm_r) %>%
  add_model(svm_m)
svm_fit <- svm_wf %>%
  fit(data)

# model summary
svm_fit %>% extract_fit_parsnip() %>% pluck("fit")
## Support Vector Machine object of class "ksvm" 
## 
## SV type: C-svc  (classification) 
##  parameter : cost C = 1 
## 
## Gaussian Radial Basis kernel function. 
##  Hyperparameter : sigma =  1.68748394282551 
## 
## Number of Support Vectors : 125 
## 
## Objective Function Value : -97.7633 
## Training error : 0.09 
## Probability model included.
# visualise the data
new_data <- expand.grid(
  X1 = seq(min(data$X1), max(data$X1), length.out = 200),
  X2 = seq(min(data$X2), max(data$X2), length.out = 200)
)

new_data  %>%
  add_column(predict(svm_fit, new_data = new_data)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=X1,y=X2,fill=.pred_class)) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(fill = "X3",
       x = "X1",
       y = "X2") +
  theme_bw() +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="G",
                              begin = 1/6,
                              end = 5/6,
                              discrete=TRUE)

# measure performance
svm_pred <- data %>%
  bind_cols(predict(svm_fit, data),
            predict(svm_fit, data, type = "prob"))
svm_pred %>% conf_mat(truth = X3,
                      estimate = .pred_class)
##           Truth
## Prediction   0   1
##          0 187  23
##          1  13 177
svm_pred %>% yardstick::roc_curve(truth = X3,
                                  .pred_0) %>%
  autoplot()

4 LDA Without Interaction Term

# fit the model
lda_r1 <- recipe(X3 ~ ., data = data)
lda_m1 <- discrim_linear() %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("MASS")
lda_wf1 <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(lda_r1) %>%
  add_model(lda_m1)
lda_fit1 <- lda_wf1 %>%
  fit(data)

# model summary
lda_fit1 %>% extract_fit_parsnip() %>% pluck("fit")
## Call:
## lda(..y ~ ., data = data)

       x = "X1",

                              begin = 1/6,
                              end = 5/6,
                              discrete=TRUE)

# measure performance

lda_pred1 %>% conf_mat(truth = X3,

7 Logistic Regression

# fit the model
lr_r <- recipe(X3 ~ ., data = data)
lr_m <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("glm")
lr_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(lr_r) %>%
  add_model(lr_m)
lr_fit <- lr_wf %>%
  fit(data)

# model summary

## 
## Call:  stats::glm(formula = ..y ~ ., family = stats::binomial, data = data)

## 
## Degrees of Freedom: 399 Total (i.e. Null);  397 Residual
## Null Deviance:       554.5 
## Residual Deviance: 554.3     AIC: 560.3
# visualise the data
new_data %>%
  add_column(predict(lr_fit, new_data = new_data)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=X1,y=X2,fill=.pred_class)) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(fill = "X3",
       x = "X1",
       y = "X2") +
  theme_bw() +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="G",
                              begin = 1/6,
                              end = 5/6,
                              discrete=TRUE)

# measure performance
lr_pred <- data %>%
  bind_cols(predict(lr_fit, data),
            predict(lr_fit, data, type = "prob"))
lr_pred %>% conf_mat(truth = X3,
                     estimate = .pred_class)
##           Truth
## Prediction   0   1
##          0 104  98
##          1  96 102
lr_pred %>% yardstick::roc_curve(truth = X3,
                                 .pred_0) %>%
  autoplot()

8 Comparing Model Performance

# get predictions
preds <- rbind(lda_pred1 %>% add_column(model = "LDA +"),
               lda_pred2 %>% add_column(model = "LDA x"),
               qda_pred %>% add_column(model = "QDA"),
               svm_pred %>% add_column(model = "SVM (RBF)"),
               lr_pred %>% add_column(model = "Logsitic Reg"))


# plot ROC curves
roc_df <- preds %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  group_map(~ yardstick::roc_curve(.x, truth = X3, .pred_0) %>% mutate(model = .y$model)) %>%
  bind_rows()

ggplot(roc_df, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = model)) +
  geom_path(size = 1) +
  viridis::scale_color_viridis(option = "D", begin = 1/6, end = 5/6, discrete = TRUE) +
  geom_abline(lty = 2) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_bw()

# auc
preds %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  group_map(~ yardstick::roc_auc(.x, truth = X3, .pred_0) %>%
              mutate(model = .y$model)) %>%
  bind_rows()
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   .metric .estimator .estimate model       
##   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>       
## 1 roc_auc binary         0.516 LDA +       
## 2 roc_auc binary         0.977 LDA x       
## 3 roc_auc binary         0.516 Logsitic Reg
## 4 roc_auc binary         0.978 QDA         
## 5 roc_auc binary         0.972 SVM (RBF)

9 Which Model Should We Choose?

The LDA model without an interaction term is clearly rubbish, as is the logistic regression model. We should notuse either of these models. It might be worth fitting a logistic regression model with an interaction term - I suspect it would perform quite well.

# assumption checking for LDA/QDA

## group 0
### X1 qqplot
qqnorm(data$X1[data$X3==0])
qqline(data$X1[data$X3==0])

### X2 qqplot
qqnorm(data$X2[data$X3==0])
qqline(data$X2[data$X3==0])

### variances and correlation
var(data$X1[data$X3==0])
## [1] 19.34399
var(data$X2[data$X3==0])
## [1] 47.76014
cor(data$X1[data$X3==0],data$X2[data$X3==0])
## [1] -0.9628308
## group 1
### X1 qqplot
qqnorm(data$X1[data$X3==1])
qqline(data$X1[data$X3==1])

### X2 qqplot
qqnorm(data$X2[data$X3==1])
qqline(data$X2[data$X3==1])

### variances and correlation
var(data$X1[data$X3==1])
## [1] 13.22029
var(data$X2[data$X3==1])
## [1] 49.84151
cor(data$X1[data$X3==1],data$X2[data$X3==1])
## [1] 0.9469879

LDA assumes multivariate normal for each group - qqplots show this assumption is reasonable. LDA also assumes constant variance/covariance structure for all groups - comparing \(cor(X_1, X_2)\) for each group shows this assumption is unreasonable. Thus, we should not use LDA.

QDA relaxes the assumption of constant variance/covariance structure, so would be a reasonable model to choose in this instance. SVM would also be a reasonable model, though its performance is marginally worse than QDA, and we may want to choose our kernel more carefully
